Experimental alpha.7 adds **bounded parallel Git LFS transfers** with a maximum/default of four workers. CLI HTTPS LFS capture and execute-new accept --lfs-workers 1..4, including a serial fallback. Controlled native Linux/Windows latency measurements supported the default: object phases improved about 2.9–3.9× and complete capture medians about 24–43% in the three synthetic profiles. These are loopback HTTPS measurements with injected delay, not Internet-bandwidth or maximum-volume guarantees; methodology/raw samples are in docs/LFS-PERFORMANCE.md.

On a worker error, queued objects stop and all started workers join before staging cleanup. User cancellation remains distinct from peer failure. Blocking HTTP calls can still take up to their existing timeout; cancellation is checked around requests and streamed reads. Windows audit directories are initialized/probed before cloning, and new LFS targets request/check EFS before plaintext writes. Reports and encrypted failure receipts use fixed stage/entry-role and safe numeric codes. No automatic retries, rollback, new destination permissions or snapshot/backup format change is introduced. Source and payload verification, private creation, disabled automation, exact atomic ref leases and encrypted receipts remain mandatory.

Alpha.6 introduced **encrypted Git LFS payload capture, offline restore and guarded migration** through the desktop and CLI. Capture is explicit: select Include Git LFS payloads or pass --include-lfs. Every supported pointer across all reachable history, including deleted historical files, must have a payload with the exact size and SHA-256. Local capture reads the standard LFS cache; HTTPS capture uses the selected repository's Batch/Basic endpoint. Hooks, .lfsconfig and custom adapters are not executed.

LFS-aware snapshots use authenticated Git manifest v3 and require alpha.6 or newer for Git restore. Existing v1/v2 snapshots and same-key vault/backup containers remain supported. Restore is offline, preserves Git pointers and populates a verified bare-repository LFS cache before no-replace publication. Guarded new-private migration validates payloads before creation, independently downloads/hash-checks uploaded objects before publishing Git refs and verifies them again from the fresh destination clone. Incomplete Git-only LFS snapshots are refused before creation. Reviewed counts and encrypted receipts remain bound to the source snapshot.

Support is bounded to canonical three-line SHA-256 v1 pointers, 10,000 unique LFS objects, 10 GiB per object and 100 GiB total. Transfers stream in batches of up to 100 objects with at most four object workers. HTTPS action redirects and automatic retries are refused; repository credentials never cross origins. Nonstandard discovery, pointer extensions/legacy encodings, SSH LFS, proxies and custom/tus transfers are unsupported. Failure leaves no local published snapshot/restore; uncertain remote operations can leave payloads in the newly created private destination and require manual inspection of encrypted receipts.

This first write workflow supports personal namespaces, SHA-1 snapshots with an existing symbolic default branch, up to 128 heads/tags and 8 KiB total ref-name bytes. GitHub needs classic repo+workflow scopes; GitLab needs personal api+write_repository scopes. GitLab's new source default is protected for maintainers with force pushes disabled. No organization/group creation, existing-repository adoption, automatic retry/rollback, external submodule payload transfer or hosting issues/PR metadata transfer is included. Notes/internal refs stay in the source archive. Incomplete operations can leave a new private repository and partial data; inspect encrypted receipts rather than rerunning a consumed plan.

Existing local/HTTPS capture, full-history local restore, read-only plans, encrypted storage and portable same-identity backup recovery remain supported. Vault and backup container formats are unchanged; remote manifest v2 requires alpha.4 or newer; LFS manifest v3 requires alpha.6 or newer. No hosting token is stored in plans, archives, backups, preferences or activity. Lock clears decrypted metadata.

Installed Git 2.48+ and verified working storage are required: ext4/XFS on mounted LUKS for Linux, EFS for Windows. Linux desktop requires writable /dev/shm tmpfs for its private browser profile; Windows uses incognito WebView2. OS swap/dump policy is separate.

Choose **repo-stealer-desktop-*** for graphical installers: Linux x86_64 DEB/RPM/AppImage or Windows x86_64 NSIS setup EXE. Other packages are the CLI. SHA256SUMS is included. Source commits and version tags are SSH-signed; installers are not OS code-signed. Native Linux/Windows LFS capture/migration, reciprocal backup recovery and DEB/AppImage/NSIS workflows/version checks gate publication; desktop RPM packaging/digests are checked, while Fedora/openSUSE desktop RPM installation remains untested.

This is an experimental application without independent application security review. Read docs/GIT-LFS.md and docs/GUARDED-MIGRATIONS.md for supported credentials, exact safeguards, administrative-race boundaries and recovery instructions. Keep a verified encrypted backup.
